nodes.title: TOOL TIP - Promts per CLip
widgets_values:
using [1] ... [2] splits the promt per clip

[1] Opening → controlled camera movement

A cinematic podcast introduction featuring the same attractive adult woman. She is funny, charismatic, naturally expressive, with a warm smile and neat, small eyebrows. She speaks directly to the camera with natural eye contact.

The camera makes one slow, smooth movement toward the subject and gradually arrives at a comfortable presenter distance. The movement stops at this distance. Once the final distance is reached, the camera remains completely stationary.

Keep the entire head, hair, shoulders, and upper body comfortably visible. Plenty of space remains around her head. Never crop or cut off any part of her face or head.

[2] Hold the established distance

Continue directly from the previous shot and preserve the exact established camera distance. Do not move closer. Do not zoom in. Do not push in.

The woman continues speaking naturally to the camera in a comfortable medium presenter framing. Her entire head and shoulders remain visible with clear space around them. Natural hand gestures and facial expressions. The camera stays at the same distance for the entire shot.

[3] Slight camera adjustment, then STOP

Continue from the previous shot at the same comfortable distance. The camera may make a very subtle adjustment in position, but it must not move closer to the woman's face.

Maintain a natural presenter framing with the complete head, hair, shoulders, and some upper body visible. No zoom toward the face. No tightening of the frame. No face-filling crop. After the subtle adjustment, the camera remains completely still.

[4] Side movement only

Continue from the previous shot at the same camera distance. The camera moves gently sideways around the subject into a subtle three-quarter angle, approximately 20–30 degrees.

This is lateral movement, not forward movement. Do not move closer to her. Do not zoom in. Maintain the same comfortable framing and distance. Keep her entire head and shoulders visible with generous space around her face. After reaching the three-quarter angle, the camera stops and remains still.

[5] Final framing — NO MORE ZOOM

Continue from the previous shot with the same camera distance and framing. Do not move closer. Do not zoom in. Do not push toward the face.

The woman finishes her introduction naturally. Maintain a comfortable presenter framing with her entire head, hair, neck, and shoulders visible, plus clear space around her head. The camera remains at this distance for the entire shot. No further camera movement toward the subject. No face crop. No cut-off forehead, hair, chin, or sides of the face.

nodes.title: Tool Tip Ref image auto mode
widgets_values:
This determines what content Ref 0 represents. You need to specify in the prompt how Ref 0 should be used—for example, as the start frame (which is what I use) or for another purpose.

OFF

Only the first clip uses Ref 0 as the start frame.
Ref 0 is not used for any subsequent clips.

Last Frame

Only the first clip uses Ref 0 as the start frame.
Each following clip uses the last frame from the previous clip as its first frame.
The last frame is automatically saved to the output folder for use in the next clip.

Original

Every clip uses Ref 0 as its start frame.
Alternatively, you can define in the prompt how Ref 0 should be used.

<Subject 1> is the presenter shown in <Picture 2>, including her identity, face, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, and accessories. A cinematic podcast introduction featuring the same attractive adult woman. She is funny, charismatic, naturally expressive, with a warm smile and neat, small eyebrows. She speaks directly to the camera with natural eye contact.
Her skin look naturally soft,, and matte/dry. Maintain natural eye contact with the camera. Her expressions are lively and playful, conveying confidence, humor, and charm.

<Audio 1> is the spoken tutorial audio performed by <Subject 1>.

summary:
The target video is a realistic product tutorial featuring <Subject 1> speaking directly to the camera. <Picture 2> defines the presenter's identity and wardrobe.
retention_analysis:

detailed_description:
Realistic polished social-media podcast, filmed as one continuous presenter performance with subtle multi-camera coverage. <Subject 1> remains the same presenter shown in <Picture 2> and wears the exact wardrobe shown in <Picture 2> throughout the video.

[1] A natural medium shot establishes <Subject 1>. <Subject 1> looks toward the camera and actively delivers the tutorial using <Audio 1>. Her facial expressions naturally follow the spoken performance. The camera makes a very subtle stabilized push-in.
<Picture 1> is used as exact start frame

[2] the camera cuts to a slightly closer medium-close-up of the same <Subject 1> in the same room. <Subject 1> (S1) continues the same spoken tutorial from <Audio 1> with continuous natural lip synchronization and direct eye contact. The exact wardrobe from <Picture 2> remains unchanged. Use subtle stabilized horizontal reframing.

[3] the camera moves to a subtle close-up of <Subject 1>. She continues the same spoken tutorial and remains visibly engaged with the camera. Maintain the same identity, hairstyle, wardrobe, room, lighting, and visual continuity. Use a very gentle push-in.

[4] return to a medium framing. <Subject 1> continues speaking <Audio 1> naturally and remains the visual focus. The shot feels like another camera angle from the same continuous product tutorial recording.

[5] use a medium-close framing while <Subject 1> continues the tutorial. Preserve the same presenter, exact wardrobe, room, lighting, and natural speaking performance. Use subtle stabilized camera movement.

[6] finish on a natural medium-close shot of <Subject 1> delivering the final part of <Audio 1>. Maintain continuous visual speech synchronization until the audio ends.

widgets_values:
You can re-sample individual clips, so if you have 5 clips and clips 1 and 2 are OK but you don’t like the output of clip 3, set Start = 3 and End = 3 to re-render only that clip.

This works best when the clip immediately before the one you’re re-rendering has already been completed and its latent is saved in the output folder.

When finished, manualy clean up the H3 output and Video folders.
